summary: Modular monolith Django on AWS Elastic Beanstalk with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL as the database in US; front end: Angular, React Native.

frontend.justification: Web: An opinionated, batteries-included framework that scales to large teams. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5; strong security, which you rated 5/5; well suited to healthtech projects. Mobile: Shares JavaScript/TypeScript skills and code with the web team. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 1.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.security (strong security, which you rated 5/5).
Scored 0.8 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.maintainability (strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5).

tradeoffs: Steeper learning curve and more boilerplate than React/Vue.
JS runtime adds memory overhead on very low-end phones.
Some native modules need a development build.

backend.justification: Ships auth, admin panel, ORM and migrations out of the box. Fit for this project: team.languages includes Python; strong security, which you rated 5/5; well suited to healthtech projects; built-in admin/back-office screens.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 1.9 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).
Scored 2.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).
Excluded: Firebase (Google) lacks HIPAA attestation/BAA (compliance).

tradeoffs: Heavier per-request overhead than Go/Node for very high RPS.

database.choice: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (us-east-1 N. Virginia)
database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: ACID transactions keep patient records and appointments consistent; strong security, which you rated 5/5; well suited to healthtech projects; strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5. Data stays in us-east-1 N. Virginia to satisfy data_residency=us.

alternatives.choice: Amazon RDS for MySQL (us-east-1 N. Virginia)
alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.4 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).
Scored 5.1 points lower: time-series extension adds operations without a time-series need; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to healthtech projects).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Managed web hosting on AWS (load balancer, auto scaling, health checks) without container orchestration. Fit for this project: multi-zone deployments for 99.95%.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.2 points lower: close runner-up; the chosen option combines better with the rest of the stack.

supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database in US.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor with per-MAU pricing.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Hosted checkout keeps you in PCI DSS SAQ A scope; broad global payment methods.

alternatives.why_not: Enterprise minimums.
Fewer local methods.

tradeoffs: Gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are not part of the infra estimate.

supporting.choice: Amazon S3 (us-east-1 N. Virginia) with pre-signed uploads
supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: No egress fees, but a second vendor next to AWS.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Caches uploaded media and static assets close to users and absorbs traffic spikes. Private user uploads bypass the CDN and are served via short-lived signed links from the bucket in the residency region.

alternatives.why_not: Slower first loads for public pages and media.

supporting.justification: Runs inside the existing backend; a Redis adapter lets several instances share connections.

alternatives.why_not: Per-connection pricing for something the backend can do itself.

tradeoffs: Long-lived connections need sticky sessions or a pub/sub layer.

supporting.justification: Caches hot reads and sessions to hold p95=300ms, and doubles as the pub/sub and job-queue broker.

alternatives.why_not: No pub/sub or persistence, so it cannot double as a broker.
Every read hits the database at peak.

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, image/file processing, notifications) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android and iOS (via APNs) for booking and job-status updates.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data (no PHI: FCM is not covered by a HIPAA BAA).

supporting.choice: HIPAA programme: BAAs with every vendor that touches PHI
supporting.justification: Sign a Business Associate Agreement with the cloud provider and each PHI-handling vendor before launch, keep PHI out of logs, push payloads and analytics, and enable audit logging on every PHI store.

alternatives.why_not: HIPAA eligibility only applies to services listed under a signed BAA.

supporting.choice: AWS KMS + Secrets Manager + CloudTrail + AWS WAF
supporting.justification: Compliance controls for HIPAA, SOC2: encryption keys you control, no secrets in code, tamper-evident audit logs and a web application firewall.

alternatives.why_not: Auditors expect platform-level key management and logs.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosted server to maintain.

supporting.choice: Amazon CloudWatch + OpenTelemetry tracing + uptime checks and on-call paging
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data. 99.95% needs alerting that wakes someone up.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.
